text: Welcome to Advanced Data Science. This course adds the specializations that separate a junior candidate from a senior one, starting with the algorithm that wins most tabular-data problems today: gradient boosting.

A random forest grows many deep trees independently and averages them, which mainly reduces variance. Boosting works the opposite way: it grows many shallow trees one after another, and each new tree is trained to fix the mistakes the ensemble has made so far. Boosting mainly reduces bias.

The loop is simple. Start with a constant prediction, the average of the target. Compute the residuals, actual minus current prediction. Fit a small tree to those residuals. Add a fraction of that tree's output, controlled by the learning rate. Then repeat. For squared error, the residual is exactly the negative gradient of the loss, so fitting a tree to residuals is gradient descent in the space of functions.

On a noisy sine wave with three hundred points, test mean squared error drops from zero point five eight nine with no trees, to zero point four nine three after one tree, zero point two five five after five trees, and zero point zero five zero after fifty trees. Each tree removes a slice of the remaining error.

Scikit-learn's GradientBoostingRegressor does exactly this loop, with a few extras. Fit it with the same n_estimators, learning_rate, and max_depth as the from-scratch version, and np.allclose confirms the predictions match: the library isn't magic, it's the same algorithm, just optimized.

Three dials matter. n_estimators is how many trees; more fits training data more tightly and can eventually overfit. learning_rate is how much of each tree to add; smaller steps generalize better but need more trees. max_depth controls how complex each tree is; boosting usually prefers shallow trees, often depth three to six.

Boosting builds trees sequentially, each fitted to the errors so far, added in small steps controlled by a learning rate. You've now seen the algorithm end to end. Next up: XGBoost, the library that made gradient boosting fast and popular.
